chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Asim ibn Humayd from Abi Basir from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man gives permission to his slave to engage in trade, and debt becomes incumbent upon the slave. He said: 'If he gave him permission to incur debt, then the debt is upon the master; and if he did not give him permission to incur debt, then there is nothing upon the master, and the slave is sought out (held liable) for the debt.'
ai.seo_question: Who is liable for the debt of a slave or employee who trades with their master's permission?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of vicarious liability in commercial transactions, distinguishing between explicit permission to incur debt (making the master liable) and mere permission to trade (leaving the slave personally liable). It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the specificity of authorization (idhn) in determining financial responsibility, a key concept in usul al-fiqh regarding agency and representation.
